A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IIS/IISA and WIISA research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections S1–S5 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original crowdsourced annotations for 785 images, annotation-reliability analyses, predictive-model experiments and ablations, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds attention-map case studies of WIISA-trained TOPIQ in Section S2.5 and Figure S6.

M1.justification: WIISA retains the same scale sampling, Lanczos downscaling, Equation (2) weak-label generation and training-batch augmentation. The new attention maps analyze the existing TOPIQ model without changing its architecture or prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 785-image IISA-DB, pretraining datasets and supplementary dataset analyses. The attention examples concern existing natural-image coverage; text-heavy images are discussed as unexplored rather than evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2 and S1 retain the same comparators. Section 6.2 changes QualiCLIP to QualiCLIP+, but both versions describe prompt learning and retain identical QualiCLIP table entries, supporting a naming clarification rather than a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: Section S2.5 introduces qualitative inspection of WIISA-trained TOPIQ attention on two images using the visualization method cited from TOPIQ. Existing quantitative evaluation settings, including splits, metrics, preprocessing and multi-scale sampling, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section S2.5 and Figure S6 probe attention to focused foreground objects and semantic objects surrounded by texture. The existing weak-label-count, threshold and interpolation ablations, and the quality-versus-scale assumption analysis, are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain ten cross-validations with median test performance, 100-resample annotation bootstrapping with 95% confidence intervals, and 200 inter-group comparisons with standard-deviation reporting. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and S1 are unchanged; TOPIQ Base/WIISA SRCC remains 0.764/0.808. Figure S6 adds the qualitative finding that attention concentrates on focused and semantically salient regions.

T1.justification: The IIS definition, monotonicity assumptions, weak-label derivation in Equations (1)–(2), supplementary sensitivity definition and geometric-mean derivation in Equation (S1) are retained. No mathematical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: defining IIS/IISA, constructing IISA-DB, and proposing WIISA to improve adapted IQA models. Their scientific scope and central performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section S2.5 interprets attention maps as suggesting that degradation of semantic content drives IIS predictions. Section S4 newly specifies the focus on low-level distortions in user-generated images and cautions that applicability to text-heavy images with readability-based quality remains unexplored.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise of release upon acceptance with a repository link and a statement that code, data and pretrained models are available. Existing crop, augmentation, interpolation and hardware disclosures in Section S3.1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al.'s High Resolution Image Quality Database reference and cites it in Section S3.2, replacing an unresolved citation alongside KonX. The QualiCLIP reference title changes but retains the same authors and arXiv identifier; broader research positioning is stable.

P1.justification: Several passages in the introduction, related work and method explanation are tightened or rephrased, with small terminology and acknowledgment edits. Section S2.5 and the domain-limitation paragraph are added, while the overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the attention-map Figure S6 and moves the existing image-example grid from Figure S6 to Figure S7. Existing figures and tables are resized or repositioned, including Tables 2 and S1, without changing their underlying graphical content or table structures.

improvement.justification: v3 provides concrete resource-access instructions, adds illustrative attention evidence, and explicitly identifies an untested application boundary for text-heavy images. These improve usability and interpretation modestly; the central method, quantitative evidence and theoretical support remain unchanged.
